title: IFERROR replaces #N/A when a new vendor isn't on the master yet

hook.body:
with #N/A down the
cost center column

payoff.headline:
LABEL THE MISS
YOURSELF
payoff.sub: Worth doing once you're confident the lookup itself is sound.

script.vo: You send the coding file over, and there's an #N/A sitting in the cost center column.
AP invoices waiting to be coded.
script.caption:
AP invoices waiting
to be coded.

script.vo: The vendor master is right below.
script.caption:
Vendor master
sits right below.

script.vo: Ordinary VLOOKUP, exact match, pointed at the master.
script.caption:
Ordinary VLOOKUP.
Exact match.

script.vo: Brightline Freight is a new vendor. One row, one #N/A.
script.caption:
New vendor.
No row to find.

script.vo: The formula's doing its job. There's just no row to find.
script.caption:
Formula's fine.
The row doesn't exist.

script.vo: So wrap the lookup in IFERROR and hand it the words you want in place of the error.
script.caption:
Wrap it in *IFERROR*.
Hand it your own words.

script.vo: Spell it out for whoever reads the file next.
script.caption:
Spell it out for
the next reader.

script.vo: Fill down, and every vendor that is on the master still comes through.
script.caption:
Vendors on the master
still come through.

script.vo: Worth knowing, IFERROR hides a typo or a broken reference just as quietly.
script.caption:
IFERROR hides typos
and bad references too.

script.vo: So save it for a lookup you already trust.

post.title: Replace #N/A when a vendor isn't on the master yet
post.description:
how to replace #N/A in a vlookup when the vendor isn't in the list
Wrap the lookup in IFERROR and give the miss a label, or use two empty quote marks if you want the cell blank. Save this one.
